description: RIFT Planck TT likelihood comparison (Phase 5b). Uses approximate full-sky Gaussian TT likelihood against Planck 2018 best-fit theory spectrum (COM_PowerSpect R3.01). chi2 = f_sky * sum_l (2l+1) * [x - 1 - ln(x)], x = (D_l^pred + N_l) / (D_l^Planck + N_l). When D_l^pred = D_l^Planck, x=1 and chi2=0 (correct baseline). Closes final CMB referee gap.

LCDM.interpretation: LCDM chi2 > 0 because CLASS uses Planck params but the theory file is the published best-fit (tiny numerical differences and lensing scheme). The LCDM residual sets the baseline noise floor for comparison.

comparison.interpretation: Delta_chi2 = chi2_RIFT - chi2_LCDM = +906.85. This corresponds to 30.1-sigma CMB tension from RIFT's BAO best-fit parameters. PHYSICAL INTERPRETATION: The RIFT BAO best-fit (H0=68.14, Omega_m=0.294) shifts the CMB acoustic peaks relative to the Planck LCDM best-fit (H0=67.36, Omega_m=0.315). The CMB is exquisitely sensitive to these shifts across l=2-2500, so even a 3.4% RMS C_ell deviation (vs. 0.26% for LCDM) accumulates to a large chi2 over thousands of modes. IMPORTANT CONTEXT: (1) This is NOT a test of the RIFT field equations — it tests only whether the RIFT BAO best-fit *parameters* are CMB-consistent. (2) The BAO fit has a known H0-rd degeneracy: only H0*rd is constrained by BAO. The individual H0=68.14 is poorly constrained. (3) A RIFT cosmology with parameters jointly fit to CMB+BAO could find a lower-tension solution (Lambda0 modifies the background, allowing different H0/Omega_m). (4) The LCDM baseline chi2=6.2 confirms the formula and reference spectrum are correct. (5) This tension is analogous to the standard cosmological H0+Omega_m tension between CMB and BAO in LCDM — RIFT does not eliminate this tension with BAO-only parameters. PAPER RECOMMENDATION: Report this result honestly. Discuss that the BAO-only best-fit is parameter-degenerate, and that a joint CMB+BAO RIFT fit is the proper resolution (future work).
comparison.physical_interpretation_note: chi2_RIFT / n_modes = 1.88e-4 << 1. The per-mode chi2 is tiny, confirming the deviation is small in any given mode. The large total chi2 (913) comes from coherent contributions across ~4.9 million f_sky-weighted modes. This is a signal-integration effect, not a large per-mode discrepancy. The 3.4% RMS C_ell deviation (vs Planck theory) is the relevant measure of RIFT cosmological parameter tension.
